query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A deep neural network (DNN) potential trained on ab initio high-temperature liquid configurations of multicomponent high-entropy alloys will reduce the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 40–50% compared to traditional EAM references, due to its improved ability to capture the diverse atomic configurations present near melting temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys in the liquid state at temperatures near or just above their high melting points (approximately 0.9–1.1 Tₘ).
generation.intervention: Replace the conventional EAM reference used in thermodynamic integration with a DNN potential that is specifically trained on a comprehensive ab initio dataset of high-temperature liquid configurations, including representative data from elemental and binary systems.
generation.conditions: Applicable for refractory HEAs under high-temperature conditions near liquid–solid transitions (0.9–1.1 Tₘ), where the atomic configuration diversity is most pronounced.
generation.structural_mediator: An enhanced representation of the diverse atomic configurations and local atomic environments in the high-temperature liquid state that is enabled by the DNN potential.
generation.mechanism: By training on a broad set of ab initio data capturing the many atomic configurations of the liquid state, the DNN potential provides a reference that more accurately overlaps with the target ab initio phase-space. This reduces the mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path relative to traditional EAM-based references.
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by roughly 40–50% compared to TOR-TILD's EAM references, resulting in free-energy estimates that converge more closely with direct ab initio calculations.
generation.baseline: Free-energy calculations using TOR-TILD’s EAM references, which inadequately sample the diverse configuration space of the ab initio liquid.
generation.boundary: The proposed approach is expected to be effective primarily for refractory HEAs near their melting temperatures. Its reliability may decrease for alloys with significantly different compositions or for states outside the high-temperature liquid regime not well represented in the training data.
generation.uncertainty: While evidence from elemental, binary, and deep learning studies supports the potential improvement, the exact magnitude of the reduction in integration path mismatch (40–50%) remains uncertain and may vary with specific alloy compositions and training data coverage.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform thermodynamic integration free-energy calculations for a refractory HEA liquid near its melting point using the DNN potential as the reference. Compare the results to (a) direct ab initio free-energy calculations and (b) calculations obtained using TOR-TILD’s EAM references. The experiment should focus on monitoring the convergence and magnitude of the integration path mismatch.
measurements: Magnitude of the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch
Absolute free-energy differences at a liquid–solid transition
Convergence behavior along the integration path
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the DNN potential does not achieve an approximate 40–50% reduction in the integration path mismatch compared to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, or if the free-energy differences do not converge within the expected uncertainty bounds relative to independent ab initio benchmarks, then the hypothesis is falsified.

High-entropy alloys (HEAs) represent the most recent class of these materials with a high potential for high-temperature high-strength applications. Aside from their chemical composition and microstructure-property relationship, limited information on the effect of heat treatment as a decisive factor for alloy design is available in the literature. This work intends to contribute to this research topic by investigating the effect of heat treatment on the microstructure and mechanical performance of an Al4.4Co26Cr19Fe18Ni27Ti5.6 HEA. To analyse the formation of the coarser and more concentrated oxide particles when Mg is absent, additional microstructural observations were carried out on B2 samples sintered at temperatures between 920 °C and 1050 °C. The results obtained (Figure 17) showed that the samples sintered at 920 °C and 950 °C exhibited high homogeneity, with no visible areas with a high concentration of oxides. In contrast, in samples sintered at 980 °C and 1050 °C, oxide particles were observed at the grain boundaries, with their presence being more evident in the sample sintered at the higher temperature. Considering that the thermodynamic calculations predict the formation of a liquid phase around 950 °C, these results suggest that the coalescence and heterogeneous distribution of the oxides are promoted by the presence of this liquid phase through a mechanism that involves its segregation and preferential concentration at the grain boundaries.

The melting temperature is a crucial property of materials that determines their potential applications in different industrial fields. In this study, we used a deep neural network potential to describe the structure of high-entropy (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x carbonitrides (HECN) in both solid and liquid states. This approach allows us to predict heating and cooling temperatures depending on the nitrogen content to determine the melting temperature and analyze structure changes from atomistic point of view. A steady increase in nitrogen content leads to increasing melting temperature, with a maximum approaching for 25% of nitrogen in the HECN. A careful analysis of pair correlations, together with calculations of entropy in the considered liquid phases of HECNs allows us to explain the origin of the nonlinear enhancement of the melting temperature with increasing nitrogen content. The maximum melting temperature of 3580 ± 30 K belongs to (TiZrTaHfNb)C0.75N0.25 composition. The improved melting behavior of high-entropy compounds by the addition of nitrogen provides a promising way towards modification of thermal properties of functional and constructional materials.

The polymorphic transition from fcc to hcp unveiled in this work demonstrates that high-pressure can help overcome the kinetic barrier between hcp and fcc HEAs. Since the hcp CoCrFeMnNi HEA is more thermodynamically stable than the fcc polymorph at lower temperatures, the hcp phase can be retained after pressure release, and this hcp phase may have excellent mechanical properties at cryogenic temperatures. The polymorphic transition discovered in this work is by no means limited to this specific CoCrFeMnNi HEA, and we expect that this behaviour could be general in various HEAs at certain pressure and temperature conditions. Therefore, our results contribute to understanding of thermodynamics and kinetics in HEA systems. These materials consist of single-phase crystalline solid solutions (crystallographic order), comprised of a random arrangement of >4 metallic components in near-equiatomic proportions (chemical disorder). Such compositions were previously expected to produce multiphase alloys, consisting of brittle intermetallics; and were therefore expected to be impractical for most applications. The –TS term becomes more dominant at elevated temperatures, suggesting that high entropy phases could be particularly stable at high temperatures. AbstractThe solidification microstructures of the TiNbTaZr medium-entropy alloy and TiNbTaZrX (X = V, Mo, and W) high-entropy alloys (HEAs), including the TiNbTaZrMo bio-HEA, were investigated. Equiaxed dendrite structures were observed in the ingots that were prepared by arc melting, regardless of the position of the ingots and the alloy system. In addition, no significant difference in the solidification microstructure was observed in TiZrNbTaMo bio-HEAs between the arc-melted (AM) ingots and cold crucible levitation melted (CCLM) ingots. A cold shut was observed in the AM ingots, but not in the CCLM ingots. The interdendrite regions tended to be enriched in Ti and Zr in the TiNbTaZr MEA and TiNbTaZrX (X = V, Mo, and W) HEAs. AbstractThe third-generation thermodynamic descriptions for Ta-Cr and Ta-V binary systems were performed to construct the reliable thermodynamic database for refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) containing Laves phase. The third-generation Gibbs energy expressions of pure Cr and V in both solid and liquid phases were established, from which the thermodynamic properties and thermal vacancy can be well described. The thermodynamic descriptions of Ta-Cr and Ta-V over the whole composition and temperature regions were carried out based on the reviewed phase equilibria and thermodynamic data with the CALPHAD (CALculation of PHAse Diagrams) approach. Specifically, the thermodynamic parameters of C14 and C15 Laves phases were evaluated by combining the theoretically computed and experimentally measured thermodynamic properties as well as the semiempirical relations. The calculated phase diagrams and thermodynamic properties in Ta-Cr and Ta-V systems according to the present thermodynamic parameters had a nice agreement with the experimental data even down to 0 K, indicating the reliability of the present modeling.Keywords: third-generation thermodynamic description, Ta-Cr system, Ta-V s

The third-generation Gibbs energy expressions of pure Cr and V in both the liquid and A2 phases were established. By applying these expressions, the thermodynamic properties down to 0 K and thermal vacancy near the melting point can be well described. Besides, the lattice stability of Cr and V over the whole temperature range can be guaranteed. Based on the third-generation Gibbs energy expressions of pure elements, the Ta-Cr and Ta-V binary systems were thermodynamically assessed by considering the reviewed phase equilibria and thermodynamic data with the CALPHAD approach. A strategy to estimate the Gibbs energy of Laves phase was proposed by combining the theoretically computed and experimentally measured thermodynamic properties as well as semiempirical relation. Such a method was applied to C14 and C15 Laves phases in Ta-Cr and Ta-V binary systems. The calculated phase diagrams and thermodynamic properties showed nice agreement with the measured ones. Significant improvements can be observed at low temperatures compared with those from the second-generation thermodynamic descriptions, indicating the high reliability of the present thermodynamic descriptions.

decision.trend: Early work on high-entropy alloys largely relied on traditional Embedded Atom Method (EAM) references or similar classical potentials, which were later found to inadequately sample the complex configuration space of the high-temperature liquid phase. Over time, researchers have introduced advanced ab initio frameworks and incorporated data‐driven and active‐learning potentials (e.g., moment-tensor potentials and deep neural network potentials) to better capture the rich atomic environments inherent to these systems. These approaches have demonstrated improved phase-space sampling and more accurate free-energy predictions in elemental systems, binary alloys, and even selected multicomponent systems, yet they have not yet been implemented as a unified, single intervention for liquid-phase free-energy integration.
decision.unsolved: Despite progress, the key issue remains: a single, methodologically streamlined reference potential that sufficiently represents the myriad ab initio liquid configurations in multicomponent HEAs is missing. In particular, existing EAM-based methods (e.g., TOR-TILD’s references) still suffer from thermodynamic-integration path mismatches, especially in the high-temperature regime and for compositions with significant configuration diversity.
decision.lever: Develop a deep neural network (DNN) potential trained specifically on high-temperature liquid configurations of multicomponent HEAs, including representative data from elemental and binary systems. The key is to assemble a training set that densely samples atomic environments at temperatures near (0.9–1.1 Tₘ) and over compositions typical of refractory alloys, so that the DNN potential can be used as the reference in thermodynamic integration.
decision.why: A DNN potential offers the flexibility to capture a far wider range of atomic configurations than conventional EAM models, directly addressing the phase-space overlap deficiency. Drawing on evidence from recent deep learning melting simulations and ab initio optimization frameworks, we predict that such a model could reduce the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by roughly 40–50% relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references. A decisive test would be to benchmark the free energy for a well-characterized liquid–solid transition; if the DNN-based integration fails to converge on the ab initio free-energy difference within expected uncertainty bounds, the hypothesis would be falsified.
